summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and diabetes was admitted for persistent substernal chest pain unresponsive to nitroglycerin. Initial evaluation showed no EKG changes or troponin elevation, but due to high cardiac risk and ongoing symptoms, he underwent an exercise stress test that revealed reduced exercise tolerance and symptoms during recovery. A cardiac catheterization confirmed two-vessel coronary disease with a significant blockage in the LAD, leading to placement of a drug-eluting stent and PTCA. He also received an extra hemodialysis session for volume overload and was transfused for anemia. A urinary tract infection with hematuria was treated with antibiotics, and outpatient urology and podiatry follow-ups were arranged for hematuria and a chronic toe ulcer. Blood pressure was managed with uptitrated lisinopril and metoprolol. He was discharged home in stable condition with updated medications and clear follow-up instructions.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Ulcer of other part of foot
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
